name: BTS5090-1EJA
title: PROFET+ 12V BTS5090-1EJA: single-channel 90 mΩ smart high-side power switch
summary: A one-channel high-side switch for 12 V automotive loads: an N-channel vertical power DMOS with a charge pump, in an 8-pin PG-DSO-8-43 EP with the supply on the exposed pad. On-resistance is 90 mΩ typical at 25 °C and 180 mΩ at most at 150 °C; nominal load current is 3 A, and loads named for it are lamps up to one P21W bulb and LEDs. It limits current, shuts down and restarts on overtemperature, clamps inductive kick-back at about 47 V, and reports load current as a proportional current on the IS pin (ratio 1460 typical) or a fixed fault current, enabled by DEN. Logic inputs work from 3.3 V and 5 V, and the logic ground is separate from load ground.

circuits.title: Application diagram
circuits.description: The switch drives a lamp at the end of a cable from a battery feed that also comes in through a cable. A microcontroller drives IN and DEN through 4.7 kΩ resistors and reads the sense current as a voltage across RIS, through RSENSE and RA/D with a 7 V Zener and a 100 pF filter at its A/D input. The device ground goes to module ground through RGND in parallel with diode D. A 36 V bidirectional Zener and 100 nF sit across the supply; RPD and COUT0 load the output, and the PNP T1 with ROL pulls the output up from VS for the open-load-in-OFF check. The microcontroller's own ground is kept apart from the module ground that carries the load return.

operation.text: The output transistor is an N-channel vertical DMOS driven by a charge pump. RDS(ON) rises with junction temperature and climbs steeply below about 6 V of supply (Figure 8). A high level on IN turns it on with a controlled slope chosen for low EMC emission.

tON_delay runs from the IN edge to 10% of VS on the output and tON to 90%; tOFF_delay runs from the falling IN edge to 90% and tOFF to 10%. Slew rates are measured between 30% and 70% of VS (Figure 9).

At turn-off of an inductive load the output swings below ground. A clamp ZDS(AZ) between VS and OUT holds it at VS - VDS(AZ), so the transistor does not avalanche, but the energy goes into the chip and the allowed inductance is limited: equations (1) and (2) give the energy and Figure 12 the single-pulse limit, 50 mJ at 3 A from TJ = 150 °C.

When OUT is driven above VS, current IINV flows back to VS through the body diode (2.5 A typical capability). The output follows IN, except that an OFF-to-ON change of IN during inverse current keeps it off until the inverse current has gone. With the channel off the diagnosis shows open load in OFF; with it on, open load in ON, and the overtemperature signal is blocked. A spurious diagnosis can appear when VINV first arrives; afterwards and when it vanishes the diagnosis is valid. No protection works during inverse current.

If the module ground is lost while the load stays grounded, the channel turns off, or stays off, whatever IN does. For loss of the device ground, series resistors between the microcontroller and the inputs are recommended so the channel is sure to turn off. A current IOUT(GND), 0.1 mA typical at VS = 28 V, can still flow out of OUT. ZGND, the ground network, may be a resistor or a diode.

Below VS(UV) the switch is off. Above VS(OP) it can be turned on; between the two it can stay on but not necessarily switch. While on, the protections work, but diagnosis is guaranteed only with VS inside VNOM, 8 V to 18 V (Figure 15).

An internal Zener ZD(AZ) clamps the logic supply; a ground resistor must limit its current. Above VS(AZ) the power transistor turns on and the internal ground rises to VS - VS(AZ), and IN and DEN, through their ESD Zeners, follow toward that level depending on what drives them. A channel that was on stays on; one that was off may turn on. Between VBAT(SC) and VDS(AZ) the output still follows IN, but with the channel on the figures are no longer guaranteed and life, short-circuit robustness and EAS capability are reduced. A 150 Ω resistor as ZGND gives better results than a diode with 1 kΩ (Figure 16).

With the battery reversed the body diode conducts, the load limits that current, and the device dissipates power. Ground and logic-pin currents must be held to the absolute maximum ratings with resistors: RGND limits the Zener current, RIN and RDEN the logic and ESD-stage current, RSENSE the sense transistor current (it then behaves as a diode). Recommended: RIN = RDEN = RSENSE = 4.7 kΩ; ZGND a 150 Ω resistor, or a Schottky diode with 1 kΩ in parallel when overvoltage is not a concern, optionally with a parallel capacitor for EMC. No protection works under reverse polarity (Figure 17).

Overload such as a cold lamp filament's inrush, or a short to ground, is first met by limiting current to IL(SC), which depends on VDS: typically 30 A up to 15 V, falling to 15 A at 20 V and staying there to 28 V (Figure 18). The DMOS heats while limiting, which also changes the current.

Each channel has an absolute sensor, TJ(SC), and a dynamic one that trips on a rise of ΔTJ(SW). Either turns the channel off, and it stays off until the temperature has fallen enough; then it turns on again if IN is still high, so a lasting overload cycles (Figure 19). ΔTSTEP is the heating caused by the overcurrent.

IS delivers a sense current IIS. With DEN low IS is high-impedance; with DEN high the sense is on. Without a hard fault (short to GND, current limit, overtemperature, excessive dynamic temperature rise, or open load in OFF) IIS equals IL / kILIS, with accuracy depending on temperature and current; on a hard fault IS gives IIS(FAULT).

A pull-down RIS on IS turns the current into a voltage; it must be over 560 Ω to keep sense-circuit losses down, and 1.2 kΩ is typical. For better accuracy near half of IL(NOM) the ratio can be calibrated once in the application: kILIS is allowed to drift by ΔkILIS (±5 %) from a single point taken at IL3 and TJ = 25 °C, which narrows the spread across temperature and supply (Figure 22).

With the channel on, a load current below IL(OL) (leakage through an open load, for instance from humidity) gives a sense current under IIS(OL); above it the sense current is at least IIS(OL) (Figure 24).

A pull-up ROL from the output to the supply is recommended, sized against all leakage (IL(OFF) plus outside leakage from humidity or corrosion) and the threshold VOL(OFF). A switch SOL in series with ROL keeps standby current down. With the channel off and the load missing the output rises nearly to VS; the device reads this as open load and IS switches to IIS(FAULT). An extra RPD pulls the output to 0 V, otherwise it floats, and also serves short-to-battery detection (Figure 25).
For an open-load-in-OFF request, at least tsIS(OT_BLANK) must pass between the falling edge of IN and the rising edge of DEN; otherwise VOUT is not settled and the diagnosis may be wrong (Figure 26).

A short from OUT to VS diverts some or all of the load current, so the sense current falls below normal. The open-load-in-OFF circuit can also detect the short, using a resistor RSC_VS from the output to ground (Figure 27).

operation.topic: Sense during overload and inverse current
operation.text: Overload means the current reaches its limit, the temperature rise ΔTJ(SW) trips, or TJ reaches TJ(SC); with DEN high IS then gives IIS(FAULT). During thermal restart cycling IS stays at IIS(FAULT) rather than toggling. Under inverse current the channel reports open load, in OFF or in ON.

IN and DEN have the same structure: a threshold input with a Schmitt trigger and hysteresis, compatible with 3.3 V and 5 V microcontrollers and with PWM. The output is either on or off, never linear. The switching point lies in the band from the VIN(L) maximum to the VIN(H) minimum; where in that band depends on process and temperature. An unused input is left open or tied to device ground, not module ground, through a resistor.

RthJA uses a JEDEC 2s2p FR4 board, 1.5 mm thick, 70 µm outer and 35 µm inner copper, with 0.3 mm thermal vias under the exposed pad reaching the first inner layer (Figure 4). The thermal impedance board has 600 mm² of cooling area (Figure 5). The 1s0p curves use a single layer with the footprint only, 300 mm² or 600 mm².
The typical curves come from 3 lots of 3 devices each, measured at 8 V, 13.5 V and 18 V across temperature. A curve with no supply dependence is the 13.5 V curve.
